proofs.proof_tex:
\begin{proof}
Write
\[
\widetilde{\overline Y}
=\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(\overline Y_g),
\qquad
\widetilde m=\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(m_g),
\]
in cohort-major order, and define
\[
W_{gN}
=\frac1{\sqrt{n_g}}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}(Y_{gi}-m_g),
\qquad
W_N=\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(W_{gN}).
\tag{1}
\]
Since \(n_g/N\to p_g>0\), every \(n_g\to\infty\). For an arbitrary
block vector \(a=\operatorname{col}_{g\in C}(a_g)\), the scalar
i.i.d. central limit theorem, finite second moments, and mutual
independence of the cohort samples give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E\exp\{it\,a^\prime W_N\}
&=\prod_{g\in C}
\mathbb E\exp\{it\,a_g^\prime W_{gN}\}\\
&\longrightarrow
\prod_{g\in C}
\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2}a_g^\prime\Sigma_ga_g\right\}\\
&=\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2}{2}
a^\prime\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g)a\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Hence, by the Cram\'er--Wold device,
\[
W_N\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(
0,\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g)
\right).
\tag{3}
\]
This conclusion remains valid when some \(\Sigma_g\) are singular;
the corresponding Gaussian law is then degenerate.

Let
\[
D_N=\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}
\left(\sqrt{\frac N{n_g}}\,I_T\right),
\qquad
D=\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}
\left(p_g^{-1/2}I_T\right).
\tag{4}
\]
Share convergence gives \(D_N\to D\), while
\[
\sqrt N(\widetilde{\overline Y}-\widetilde m)=D_NW_N.
\tag{5}
\]
Slutsky's theorem therefore yields
\[
\sqrt N(\widetilde{\overline Y}-\widetilde m)
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(
0,\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g/p_g)
\right).
\tag{6}
\]
Finally, the untreated--treated ordering is obtained from the
cohort-major ordering by the fixed stacking matrix \(\Pi\):
\[
\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)
=\Pi\sqrt N(\widetilde{\overline Y}-\widetilde m).
\tag{7}
\]
Applying the continuous mapping theorem to (6) proves
\[
\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Omega),
\qquad
\Omega
=\Pi\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}
(\Sigma_g/p_g)\Pi^\prime.
\]
\end{proof}

proposed.condition: \(\bigl\{\sigma(Y_{gi}:1\le i\le n_g):g\in C\bigr\}\) are mutually independent.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The finite collection of cohort-sample sigma-fields must be mutually independent; pairwise independence does not suffice to factor their joint characteristic function.

proposed.statement:
Let \(C\) be finite. Under independent sampling across cohorts, i.i.d. sampling within each cohort, \(n_g/N\to p_g>0\), and \(\mathbb E_P\|Y_g\|_2^2<\infty\), the stacked cohort sample means satisfy
\[
\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Omega),
\qquad
\Omega=\Pi\operatorname{blockdiag}_{g\in C}(\Sigma_g/p_g)\Pi^{\prime}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the mismatched cited-source metadata while preserving the claim and dependencies; the accompanying paper-owned proof establishes the lemma and the pipeline derives proved status.

prose_updates.tldr: At fixed \(T\), with a never-treated cohort, positive multiplicative untreated means, mutually independent cohort samples, arbitrary within-unit dependence, and finite fourth moments, one weighted tangent restriction arises from each untreated graph cycle. Bounded score truncation followed by an exact mean adjustment proves tangent completeness in the explicitly mean-differentiable experiment. The canonical gradient removes the covariance projection of the cohort-mean PPML influence onto the \(q\) cycle directions; a feasible cycle-projection estimator attains the bound and supports pointwise Wald inference. The cohort-mean PPML estimator is efficient for every bounded legal covariance law exactly when \(q=0\); for \(q>0\), exactly \(q\) primitive balances characterize its exceptional efficient laws, and a bounded strictly positive fixed-support family has exact loss \(\Gamma>0\). On the balanced equal-weight, no-covariate, no-offset intersection with Moreau--Kastler, the individual and cohort-mean point estimators coincide, so the same family and the regular cycle-projection competitor prove that the published individual estimator is not universally efficient when \(q>0\). This transfer is one-way: it gives neither the richer individual-level efficiency bound nor a \(q=0\) efficiency conclusion there. The regularized frontier for growing \(T\) and \(q\) remains open at \(\mathrm{oeq{:}growing\text{-}cycle\text{-}frontier}\).

sampling_model.units: Within each \(g\in C\), \(n_g\) units are independent and identically distributed; the finite collection \(\{\sigma(Y_{gi}:1\le i\le n_g):g\in C\}\) of cohort-sample sigma-fields is mutually independent, and \(n_g/N\to p_g>0\).
